#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides
#                              it) matches this grep -E pattern -- the hook
#                              for fixtures that verify a result INSIDE the
#                              ROI and print a verdict (code after the exit
#                              marker never runs on the vsim leg).
#   ILM_SIZE / DLM_SIZE  LM content transport override, in bytes. Unset =
#                        probe $VSIM_BIN --describe (mirrors the driver's
#                        wiring); 0 = force that memory's transport OFF
#                        (negative-control knob).
#   CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1  assert the vsim leg dumped its exit-time LM
#                        content next to its state file AND that it equals
#                        the entry-time content byte-for-byte (valid for a
#                        ROI that does not WRITE the TCM -- closes the
#                        transport loop through the real RTL SRAM).
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
# mktemp names carry no dots, so the .* globs match exactly the legs'
# sidecars (state.ilm/.dlm today, any future suffix for free).
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_QEMU".* \
            "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_VSIM".* "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()

# LM/HVM content transport (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm, ROADMAP_hvm): mirror the
# driver's run_plan wiring. The engine's --describe reports its memories in
# BYTES; when a size is > 0 the QEMU plugin drains that memory's content to
# a sidecar next to the state file and the vsim leg backdoor-loads it
# (--ilm/--dlm/--hvm). An engine without the memory (or an older binary
# whose --describe lacks the field) adds nothing. ILM_SIZE/DLM_SIZE/HVM_SIZE
# env override the probe; 0 forces that memory's transport off
# (negative-control knob).
#
# QEMU's memory GEOMETRY is synced separately and ALWAYS (lm_geom, from the
# engine's describe -- the raw analog of the driver's
# --print-qemu-config/-readconfig sync), so a transport-off negative still
# runs the guest against the engine's real geometry. This matters twice:
# QEMU's compiled-in ILM default is 2 MB at 0x0, which SHADOWS the program
# image at 0x100000 the moment a guest sets milmb.EN (the engine's real
# 64 KB ends at 0xFFFF); and QEMU's HVM default is 1 BYTE
# (hvm_size_pow_2=0), which would fault an HVM fixture's fill outright.
# Probe the engine's real sizes ONCE; lm_geom always uses these, while the
# *_SIZE transport knobs default to them but may be overridden (0 = the
# negative-control off switch).
ILM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"

ILM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)
DLM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)
HVM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size)
ILM_SIZE="${ILM_SIZE:-$ILM_REAL}"
DLM_SIZE="${DLM_SIZE:-$DLM_REAL}"
HVM_SIZE="${HVM_SIZE:-$HVM_REAL}"
VSIM_LM_ARGS=()
QEMU_LM_ARGS=()
lm_geom() {  # $1 ilm|dlm|hvm, $2 engine bytes ("" or 0 = engine has none)
  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  if [ "$1" = hvm ]; then
    # QEMU's HVM geometry property is a power of two, not bytes.
    local p=0 v=$2
    while [ "$v" -gt 1 ]; do v=$((v >> 1)); p=$((p + 1)); done
    QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=hvm_size_pow_2,value=$p")
  else
    QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=$1_size,value=$2")
  fi
}
lm_wire() {  # $1 ilm|dlm|hvm, $2 size in bytes ("" or 0 = transport off)
  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,$1_size=$2"
  VSIM_LM_ARGS+=("--$1" "$STATE_QEMU.$1")
}
lm_geom ilm "$ILM_REAL"
lm_geom dlm "$DLM_REAL"
lm_geom hvm "$HVM_REAL"
lm_wire ilm "$ILM_SIZE"
lm_wire dlm "$DLM_SIZE"
lm_wire hvm "$HVM_SIZE"
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
# timeout: a guest that wedges pre-marker (e.g. a TCM overlay shadowing its
# own image) would otherwise hang this leg forever -- QEMU runs at MHz, so
# the vsim-leg budget is generous here.
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  "${QEMU_LM_ARGS[@]}" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_LM_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# LM/HVM exit-dump check: vsim dumps its ILM/DLM/HVM content next to the
# handoff-out state file; for a ROI that never writes those memories, the
# exit bytes must equal the entry bytes -- one byte-exact loop through
# plugin drain -> sidecar -> backdoor load -> RTL SRAM -> exit dump.
if [ "${CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  for pair in "ilm:${ILM_SIZE:-0}" "dlm:${DLM_SIZE:-0}" "hvm:${HVM_SIZE:-0}"; do
    kind="${pair%%:*}"; sz="${pair##*:}"
    [ -n "$sz" ] && [ "$sz" -gt 0 ] || continue
    if [ ! -f "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim did not dump $STATE_VSIM.$kind at exit"
      exit 1
    fi
    if ! cmp -s "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind"; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: $kind exit content differs from entry content:"
      cmp "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" | head -3
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  echo "[$FIXTURE lm-exit] PASS: exit LM/HVM content matches entry byte-for-byte"
fi

# In-ROI verdict check: the guest printed its result on the vsim leg's UART.
if [ -n "${CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT:-}" ]; then
  if grep -qE "$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT" "$SIM_LOG"; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE vsim-stdout] PASS: matched '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
  else
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim output did not match '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
    echo "--- sim log (tail) ---"
    tail -25 "$SIM_LOG"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"
